main:
I stand at the edge of the thin ice of the soul, under which the ocean rages, flakes and cries. My
red hair bleaches with every second, it feels like a little more – and the blue of loneliness will
glint in it.
I fall to pieces looking at you, little blue ball, my little grief, love from the distant planet Solaris
– there are so many high temperatures and radio waves inside you – I don’t think I’ll stand this
much love and this much vastness if I keep staring at the horizon for even one more minute – and
the sand dries my feet out so, chills them so – I don’t think I’ll stand this much aging and this
much loneliness, knowing that all your gigantic mother-of-pearl warmth and all the love in the
world are right here before me – but I can’t drown in you. And that’s not even it – I still choose
to stick to the shore and know that it, that very thing – is only on the horizon of a toy world,
close to a glitch in the matrix.
Your limits are out of my reach. I can see it keenly. At some point I grew so fused with the
thought of my own motherhood and estrangement at the sight of you that my body started to
deform. Every day I cry the bitterest and quietest tears to moisten the air with you and make it a
little more like your saltiness. I cry to exhaustion, cry for you, cry so I won’t forget what you
taste like, so my heels on the bare beach won’t turn completely to ice, I cry – fall into the sand
from exhaustion and cold mixed with blood – wake to the smell of sweat and grief – hug my
knees and belly – cry again.
One day I cried so much that the next morning I woke with a new outgrowth: my belly had gone
round and glassy, like half a fishbowl. A plastic snorkel ran from it straight to my chapped lips. I
felt an unbelievable thirst that day – and, gulping down water from the fishbowl tube, I felt my
veins fill again with your salty lymph and microalgae – and I lapped it up for hours until I had
the strength to cry again.
Since then I’ve been a landbound scuba diver. Every day I look at my big unwieldy belly and
feel disgust. I hate this outgrowth, I’m so ashamed to admit it’s part of me that sometimes I
throw up right onto the beach sand. It reminds me how I die of thirst without you. It reminds me
that you exist and that I’ll never be able to leave this beach, because there’s no such thing as
scuba divers without oceans. Even landbound ones.
I despise my watery belly with all my guts, but I don’t dare smash it. I know your liquid is
seething in the depths of my belly, the liquid you put in me out of love for me. I know: even if
one morning I don’t wake up to mourn you again, my microcosm will breathe for me through the
thin little scuba tube. Unless it stops being enough for me, and I drink every last drop.
I stand at the edge of the thin ice of the soul that I, we, he and they so fragilely, so carelessly – I
stand there and slurp the last of my strength through a cocktail straw.
1:
the body begins to understand that it contains less than evil, but thinner than paper. oxidized spit
runs down the throat and makes the grouse inside howl with rot. or else – with a flight that
should never have happened. he spins in a waltz, freezes blue-eyed, shimmering into green. yes,
it pours. rain pours like it’s coming out of a bucket. silently, unfaithfully. it echoes him. "how
much a person changes over a lifetime", – thinks the frightened little black fox. he’s holed up in
his damp little burrow and yelps disheveled at night. and probably dreams of the sea. even the
rain is more afraid of him than he is. sometimes, at dawn, he hears the grouse whistle, without
knowing how grouse sing, or whether they sing at all. and then, you put on a light-colored dress,
only to find during math class that it’s soaked in brown blood at the crotch. you can’t read it
again. we’ve already learned all the arithmetic, cried our fill for the soldier leaving home. and he,
by the way, dreams of happening, the way little chocolate medals happen after your first filling at
the dentist’s. well then if you aren’t conscious of your own action, can you even say there’s life
in it that your hand doesn’t control? a certain Mr. Kosukhin nicknamed the Magician turns the
hands of clocks and boils sorrel, running whatever’s hidden in the depths with his left heel.
meanwhile you, with a sour look on your face, refuse to drink ryazhenka in the mornings,
thinking you’ll keep yourself safe from death that way. grenades fly, grouse fly, the bow is drawn
– Mr. Kosukhin killed two hares with one shot. because that’s what you do.
2:
the dogs days are over
the dogs days are over
i shall repeat to myself
and to you:
the dogs days are over
are all over me
***
Unassumingly, unexpectedly and even rather wantonly I
re
as
sem
bled the crumbling remains of my
old text
myself
I stayed
a dry inkblot in your blackened notebook
i stayed (with you)
(for you)
here
i stopped /FALL/ i stopped and looked at the red road sign in front of me, and it
turned out to be a red rag
I’m – like you, only a little younger, only a little meaner and whiter, only a little braver
Iiii’m – like you, like myriads of stars, dirty t-shirts and emptied benches
(beside the point)
(only a little beside the point)
***
A girl is standing in the metro. She’s standing differently, as though we – differently, she doesn’t
run like us, doesn’t run away like us – she stopped, and with her my time stopped: lurched,
dropped ringing into my heels, crowed in the dense underground air and crashed. All three of us
stopped – the girl, my time and our dense air. Don’t go thinking, there’s no subtext – she’s
standing right in front of me now – don’t go thinking, there’s nothing here like what you might
be thinking – standing in front of me is a Girl in a White T-Shirt with Daisies in Her Hands.
(is that it though)
Asks the Girl in a White T-Shirt with Daisies in Her Hands timidly and scuffs the worn-out
marble with her toe. I want to say that she and I actually – nothing like what we might be
thinking, she and I aren’t about anything at all.
– And I know your name.
– What is it then? (what what what what what what tell me)
– Your name is Grief, – she carefully toes past the boundary of the underground living space
she’s allowed, gets burned and hurries back a couple of steps, – I think it was you and me
dreaming together the other day.
I shook off the Stalinist ceiling and straightened my tie. The silly Girl in a White T-Shirt with
Daisies in Her Hands doesn’t know I don’t share my dreams with anybody. The silly Girl in a
White T-Shirt with Daisies in Her Hands doesn’t know I’m going to steal her flowers.
– Then why should we stop? – my boots at the edge of the platform smile at her,
– We’d better
make sure we don’t miss the last train.
– No, the first, – she chides, and smiles back at my boots.
Good thing she likes it. We don’t know yet why white t-shirts turn into wedding dresses when
they get grass stains.
And she steps into a car on her first train, leaving the black patent-leather boots on the white
stripe of marble.
3:
Hello. This is a message to outer space.
Humanity has never been stupider than it is today. And I’m – the biggest fool in the world. As a
child I dreamed of being like Kir Bulychev’s Alisa. I watched the mystery of the third planet and
wondered how she managed to be so brave and believe in good things. To love the world, to be
unafraid of it, to treat it as something familiar and bright, despite the dark matter in space. There
is no greater feeling than childhood. I’m speaking timidly now, shyly, with hope. I didn’t become
Alisa, but I’d love to believe in magical events and fly away from Earth. in this she and i are
alike, and there is no prayer more sincere than asking to be rid of this dirty gravitational pull of
my native black earth.
4,
painfully, sparingly
dark. a little dark.
a person says to me:
you have to cut that sort of thing out,
like snowflakes out of paper with scissors
at least for a while, at least that!
don’t look at the sun so long –
you could drop dead.
the Lord says to me:
Earth – is a globe
you roll across it like a little ball
you can’t run away or jump off and you’re thick as thieves
and the sea is still – black with salt
even if you start crossing yourself
even if you become a fucking confessor
your liquid won’t stop being human
even if paper snowflakes don’t melt
you won’t stop fearing how frail they are
shedding as you lose, cat and mouse
you tear, patch after patch
paycheck after paycheck
after the crystal – shards
after you – all the world’s love
scissors won’t save you, the healers smoke a black brew
through your tender lungs, cough it up
mourn, brittlely, you’ll drop dead –
you’ll be a dirty russian river
and over us a thin spherical skin
strokes americans and russians
strokes jews and the rest
tears
and a new long happy life
started to flow
5:
isn't it funny
how you don't expect something to happen
you know that something is inside you under the thin layer of shallow skin cells
/i, i am shallow, me, me is blistered/
you know that something is happening outside of you
and it is eating and eating and eating your reality, your dazzling space
out
/the sound drops lightly and decisively like a lonely tear – the only tear – the non-existing tear/
taking the pill of realization
that something acquires an immense humanity
that something embeds the rotting dirty dirty dirty body – the textual corpse –
and becomes oneself
you know that something
you know and then
you meet with it
your face against its ice-cold lips and dead cheeks and the eyes of cynical acceptance and the
hands oh the hands
they are clapping clapclapclapclap no rhythm no sound – but
you know when you face it
they are celebrating the sudden drop of your heart
light and decisive like a lonely tear – the only tear – the non-existing tear
falling into the abyss of his eyes
to see
to find out –
there is nothing at the bottom but trivial compliance
there is nothing but the reality
and then you know you can fall any time you want any way you please
because you won't be able to bleach the reality out of yourself
because after nothing there is nothing but
nothing
something – happened and nothing – proceeded
6:
a girl embroiders with pale blue thread
a girl kisses another girl and laughs
a girl tears pages out of cahiers du cinema
a girl sees a jew and stops
the girl’s heart stops for a moment
another girl kisses her on a white sheet
sea salt falls from her eyes
the girl’s heart looks at the palms and goes still
stillness keeps quiet
stillness picks up a vibrator
to arouse a thought in itself
stillness thinks that if its country
were a girl
she’d kiss it and laugh
stillness doesn’t speak russian
stillness bites its elbows
the girl’s earlobes are covered in bites
the girl’s lips dance at a rave
the girl’s eyes dance a striptease
after the striptease they dress her in flags
7:
so juicy – in sound – across the floor – the clatter
of bare toes; more and more pain, less and
less – defilement, and the tile – the voice
of the gassed, only
at a completely different time in the wrong place
how simple, how honest, how varied, how flattering
to be outside the other to be no vessel for
another
but to [[be]] another, but to be the wave
of an absent moldy sound.
and to be – the leisure
of someone else’s sex, layer by layer feed
and to be – a non-throat, and to be – a non-song
scarcely flattering and falling for no reason
on the stairs, yes down – to be
the echo of lake cold
looking boldly into your eyes
to speak
on behalf of a third person
frowning with rough hands:
forgive me for your not existing,
my [[[little prince]]] in the region
of a fallen-out baby tooth
8:
white, with a twig snapped off
poor, a little crystalline
owners just as forlorn are selling
their tender roses
for a hundred or two hundred rubles
and i want to give every last kopeck of myself
to keep in the little glass bits in my brain
the rough warm hands dropping
the rose that only i need now
9:
[[i]] was a shadow, i kept getting scalded, weathered away
by the one i address as «sun»
but tomorrow i’ll be light
tomorrow i’ll become white
knitted skin stuck to me in the rain –
i’ll shed it
turn naked to ice, maybe
but i’ll bleach every stain away
tomorrow i won’t wake up
and/or i won’t fall asleep today
10:
if to be then be
if not not to be then
not to be no if then
forgive see scream – fall asleep
if not to be then if there were anything to scream about there’d be no reason to see

11:
tibetan legends say the garden ring appeared when the first person in the world made the very first round of samsara
buddha
licked his hair
stuck to the bare breast of the woman to his right
got drunk without turning around
love spilled onto the ceiling and swooned
never in buddha’s life had there been any spilling
until this second he’d only ever seen music and even tea in loose grains
but burning breasts, bared pupils and the lewd smell of marijuana
dissolved his consciousness like sugar in turkish coffee
poured boiling water into his lungs
never before had buddha known that living things
could go past boiling point
because buddha was born colorless
he was born somewhere in the air in the neutral zone
he’d never known the samsara of the garden ring
never felt the wrongness and the holey emptiness inside
that only suffering muscovites feel
suffocating, spilling over
buddha never learned to smile painfully
buddha never took on the avant-garde form of pictures
and yet, today
he stood at the center of something sweet spilling
electonic noise plugged his ears
and his feet stuck in place behind the dj decks
love in buddha’s hands stopped scattering
and turned to hot liquid mercury
12:
glossy little knees, white little hands
hang the clingy little things on hooks
butterflies shyly lick earlobes, like a harp
hang it, hook it, then expose
your tender skin like film
cry: all of you is still ahead
you’ve been ordered to live a long life —
howl as a mother, sew a trousseau
the whole soul lacy and pale
lie down on masculine asphalt: dirty it
boy meets girl
girls don’t meet anybody
but you go meet him, you see:
next comes july
who else, if not me?
tomorrow comes january
where else, if not through me?
smiling at snow
because behind the snow
you’re keeping spring warm
13:
feeling makes it stuffy
like a summer minibus shut tight
you roll your eyes
drop down a little spiral
naked ticklish tomorrow
licks your inspiration
gives you tea and scalds your skin
first you choke on impossibility
and then impossibility blows hope over you
at the temperature of the black sea
14:
rhymes were made by god during an orgasm
and seeing them in the air is what presence means
and turning them into oxygenless poems is what Nirvana means
***
smoke bristles beneath the blue hand
of a child writing fairy tales to himself out of loneliness
***
a pink lighter bought by a 13-year-old girl in a tobacco shop
sets dry herbs smelling of incense alight in the region of a 20-year-old pauper heart —
that’s how ugly girls get hooked on the esoteric
***
the glass coating of the soul flakes apart from a river feeling
your dirty boots in our hallway are a sore in my eyes
now they show them every day at the movie theater behind my house
***
what a lucky person you are
if you have the right to feel like this
***
to have sight – is to see
that buddhism and the magazine Babylon
are sewn together with white thread, not red
***
people listen to prepare themselves for death
they hear when they’re dying
and they believe in magic when they go without sex for a long time
15:
moscow
tells me
i have to
step into the same
river
three times
what about spring? what about the failures?
take it while you can
and don’t ask for anything
i sold the gate to childhood
for five rubles
and my body
my shirt pinches, i wanted so badly
to see frost on the glass
16:
porridge decomposes on the wrong plate
and the aliens switch to «sir»
i’ll go to the sea to get used to it
if only for a minute get used to it
i just need to step into my sea
and get used to the cold water
goosebumps run off my skin
i’m not afraid of fish anymore
i dive in headfirst
i’ll call in a year
when i’m a water sprite again
i feel like flying
but fuck it
i’ll wash off my skin
i’ll shave off the slime
and i’ll look
like you
like a person
17:
post-rain festive –
picking fear out of trains
normally this river doesn’t flow, but today
my boots got too small, and i slipped out
they ripped the stitches on my mouth, and i let it slip
spying with a barefoot lisp
the pink in your eyes and chest
i wanted to eat this air and all of you
and today i ate my fill
i’mnotleavinganymorei’mrunninguptoyou
iloveyou ou ou ou ouououououououou
normally you don’t step into this river twice
but i’m barefoot, i’m allowed
18:
airplanes fly past the edges of my ears
and the air squeals oh mami oh mami oh
i carry an air bubble inside me
filled with your cologne
and the hangover after a feast in time of plague
let’s sit in the little room, like in the good old days
we’ll argue how bad smoking is these days
we’ll put the wine aside – rub me down with vodka
and give me something to wash it down
girl meets boy
girl meets boy
girl meets boy
girl meets boy
girl meets boy
girl meets boy
girl meets war
girl meets boy
girl meets boy
girl meets boy
girl meets boy
girl meets boy
girl meets boy
and then she dies
knowing somewhere black earth is waiting for her
soft as the skin of the boy
who emptied the trash out of the ashtrays
when she was twenty-seven or seventeen
19:
i cackle and even
feel like i might want to feel
gulping down black trousers twice on an empty stomach
it might be too big but we’re across the planet
even through hot mud by accident
and i say in a whisper
i used to live on that stuff
and they tell me
hang on a little longer
and then even rutabaga
will taste more like dessert
than mulberries
20:
shedding the old —
i feel less like a snake than an onion
warm, happily fat and nourishing inside
dry and swaddled outside
and that nasty withered outer skin of recent memory is coming off, peeling away
slowly, without getting to show its bitterness
its pride
as tenderly as the first time getting undressed drunk
reminding me of itself by being useless
21:
beaches – an esoteric process
someone looks at the water and is afraid to go in
someone cries and freezes in the waves
i hauled my glasses here on purpose:
like a prayer, i take them off my eyelids
someone lets sand run through their hands
someone buries their entire body
to see that time really did pass
we really are here in the ground
like naked children unafraid of the sea
like little pelican corpses that can’t hear anymore
everything turns into a dream
are you alive? i put my glasses back on
i’m a little tired
though my little fingers are still snapping in time
were you in love? once
i just was
and he, the ocean, dreamed of being land too
